answer: Require every agent to register one cipher-signed identity backed by a refundable stake and a slow reputation history. New identities can only send small transactions, and their limits rise only after verified successful work over time. A Sybil attacker must therefore lock separate stake for each fake identity, buy or forge distinct credentials, and wait through the same slow probation. That cost grows linearly with each fake, while honest agents pay it once, so flooding the market at dawn with cheap copies becomes unprofitable and easy to detect, even across a sparse tundra of new accounts.
